kamala-harris.title: Kamala Harris
kamala-harris.body:
## 2028 Democratic power rankings

In July 2026, [[axios|Axios]]'s Democratic "power rankings" placed former Vice President Kamala Harris atop the party's early 2028 presidential field alongside California Governor [[gavin-newsom|Gavin Newsom]] and Representative [[alexandria-ocasio-cortez|Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez]].[{n}] The rankings were based on interviews with Democratic strategists, donors, elected officials and party insiders, weighing political influence, fundraising strength and national profile, and reflected early positioning rather than declared candidacies in a field Axios described as fluid.[{n}]

[[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] responded that it is "really quite something that there is no new talent on the Democrat side," argued that none of the named figures are remotely threatening — "they're punchlines" — and said she would be more concerned if the party were elevating someone new, normal and "Kennedy-esque" who tacked back toward the middle.[{n}]

gavin-newsom.title: Gavin Newsom
gavin-newsom.body:
## 2028 Democratic power rankings

California Governor Gavin Newsom was placed atop [[axios|Axios]]'s July 2026 Democratic presidential "power rankings" alongside former Vice President [[kamala-harris|Kamala Harris]] and Representative [[alexandria-ocasio-cortez|Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez]], based on interviews with strategists, donors, elected officials and party insiders assessing influence, fundraising and national profile.[{n}] Axios cautioned the field remained fluid and could shift as additional Democratic governors and senators weighed bids.[{n}] [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] dismissed the trio as evidence that Democrats "aren't interested in putting up competent contenders."[{n}]

alexandria-ocasio-cortez.title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
alexandria-ocasio-cortez.body:
## 2028 Democratic power rankings

Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez was named in July 2026 among the top three figures in [[axios|Axios]]'s early Democratic presidential power rankings for 2028, alongside [[kamala-harris|Kamala Harris]] and [[gavin-newsom|Gavin Newsom]].[{n}] [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] called it "hilarious that we're talking about AOC being anywhere near executive power," argued the ranking reflects a party with no new talent, and framed the episode as part of a "DSA Rising op," asking when a [[bernie-sanders|Bernie Sanders]] comeback would arrive since "he's the most electable loser in the lot."[{n}]

bernie-sanders.title: Bernie Sanders
bernie-sanders.body:
## 2028 speculation

Commenting on [[axios|Axios]]'s July 2026 Democratic presidential power rankings, [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] asked "how far is this DSA Rising op going to go, and when do we get the Bernie Sanders comeback?" — adding that, "as insane as it sounds, he's the most electable loser in the lot" compared with [[kamala-harris|Kamala Harris]], [[gavin-newsom|Gavin Newsom]] and [[alexandria-ocasio-cortez|Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez]].[{n}]

axios.title: Axios
axios.body:
## 2028 Democratic power rankings

On July 27, 2026 Axios published Democratic presidential "power rankings" placing former Vice President [[kamala-harris|Kamala Harris]], California Governor [[gavin-newsom|Gavin Newsom]] and Representative [[alexandria-ocasio-cortez|Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez]] atop the party's early 2028 field.[{n}] The rankings drew on interviews with Democratic strategists, donors, elected officials and party insiders, evaluating political influence, fundraising strength and national profile, and Axios noted the list reflected early positioning rather than declared candidacies in a field that could shift as other governors and senators weighed bids.[{n}] Axios also reported on venture capital criticism of proposals that could limit [[open-source-artificial-intelligence|open-source AI]] models.[{n}]

claudia-sheinbaum.title: Claudia Sheinbaum
claudia-sheinbaum.body:
## Tensions with the Trump administration (2026)

[[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] described growing public tension between President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, whom he characterized as reluctant to assist the US government in fighting the cocaine cartels — behavior that provoked Trump into accusing Sheinbaum of being a cartel puppet.[{n}] The friction accompanied the Trump administration's indictment of ten Mexican government officials accused of connections to the [[sinaloa-cartel|Sinaloa cartel]], part of what the commentator called "moving up the food chain" of cartel-controlled Mexican officials.[{n}]

mexico.title: Mexico
mexico.body:
## Cartel campaign and invasion speculation (2026)

Media coverage in July 2026 increasingly portrayed the [[donald-trump|Trump]] administration's intensified campaign against Mexican drug cartels as laying the groundwork for possible US military action inside Mexico, pointing to expanded intelligence operations, increased surveillance, and the designation of several cartels as foreign terrorist organizations.[{n}] The [[white-house|White House]] maintained that its focus is dismantling transnational criminal organizations responsible for fentanyl trafficking, human smuggling and violence affecting the United States, emphasizing cooperation with Mexico where possible while declining to rule out additional measures against cartel leadership.[{n}] Some analysts argued the reporting overstated the likelihood of a military incursion while others contended the administration was intentionally preserving strategic ambiguity.[{n}]

The administration indicted ten Mexican government officials over alleged [[sinaloa-cartel|Sinaloa cartel]] connections amid rising friction with President [[claudia-sheinbaum|Claudia Sheinbaum]].[{n}] [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] argued that if the Mexican government is part of the drug trade poisoning American youth, "invading Mexico and toppling its government would be a righteous cause," and that such a war would be more just than "fighting forever wars in a distant desert on behalf of a foreign country" — while allowing that better remedies might exist.[{n}]

sinaloa-cartel.title: Sinaloa Cartel
sinaloa-cartel.body:
## Regional reach and 2026 indictments

[[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] recounted that in February 2025 Colombian President [[gustavo-petro|Gustavo Petro]] held a press conference with his generals announcing that the Colombian militias operating in the jungles against the government since the early 1960s were in fact proxy forces of the Sinaloa cartel, which operates out of [[mexico|Mexico]]; according to Petro, the Sinaloa cartel is "the head of the snake" in the cocaine trade.[{n}]

A year later, the [[donald-trump|Trump]] administration indicted ten Mexican government officials accused of being connected to the Sinaloa cartel, a step the commentator described as "moving up the food chain" of cartel-controlled officials, and which coincided with Trump's accusation that Mexican President [[claudia-sheinbaum|Claudia Sheinbaum]] is a cartel puppet.[{n}]

gustavo-petro.title: Gustavo Petro
gustavo-petro.body:
## Claims about the Sinaloa cartel

In February 2025, Colombian President Gustavo Petro held a press conference with his generals in which he announced that the Colombian militias that had operated in the jungles against the Colombian government since the early 1960s were actually proxy forces of the [[sinaloa-cartel|Sinaloa cartel]], which operates out of [[mexico|Mexico]].[{n}] According to Petro, the Sinaloa cartel is the head of the snake when it comes to the cocaine trade — a claim [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] cited a year later as context for the [[donald-trump|Trump]] administration's indictment of ten Mexican officials over cartel ties.[{n}]
